verdicts.summary: The bounded run-scope close does let markComplete fire. closeRun forks Scope.close into parentScope and only waits up to 5s for it. The new test hangs both process-scope finalizers inside a real scope finalizer and still sees the quit fiber join after TestClock.adjust(5s). The unbounded pre-close steps the note mentions are already finding 0.
verdicts.scenario: Tried the case where timeoutOption runs inside a finalizer, which is uninterruptible. The worry: the race could wait for the hung Fiber.await, so quit would still hang. The test registers stopAllPoolInstances with Effect.addFinalizer and joins the quit fiber after a 5s clock advance while both teardowns are still blocked on allowTeardown. If the timeout did not fire in an uninterruptible region, the join would hang. Caveat: the effect library source is not in the checkout and I did not run the test, so this rests on the test passing in CI. Also checked: parentScope (DesktopBackendManager.ts:648) is the instance's layer scope, which is still open while the scopedProgram finalizer runs, so the forkIn target is live. After markComplete, DesktopLifecycle.ts:131-138 calls electronApp.quit without waiting for the layer teardown.

verdicts.summary: The open hazard is that mutex acquisition (held by start during configResolve, fs exists and onPreflightFailed), onShutdown and the restart-fiber interrupt have no bound, so quit can still hang. That is exactly finding 0.
